summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation, presenting with worsening dyspnea, weight gain, and bilateral edema. His condition was complicated by a urinary tract infection with coagulase-negative staphylococcus, treated with IV ceftriaxone, and supertherapeutic INR and digoxin levels, both managed by temporary discontinuation and careful restart. He received IV furosemide and a diuretic drip, which was paused due to rising creatinine, then resumed as oral torsemide. Dobutamine was briefly used for perfusion support. His heart failure improved with diuresis, and he was transitioned to oral medications including losartan, with uptitration of hydralazine and isosorbide. He was discharged to extended care with stable vital signs, improved symptoms, and a weight of 133.6 kg.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Adverse effect of anticoagulants, initial encounter
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
